editorial:
Ever feel like your family only knows how to talk to each other through a screen or a phone? That is exactly what you get with these three sisters. Georgia, Eve, and Maddy have a messy relationship with their grumpy father, Lou. When Lou ends up in a Los Angeles hospital and might actually die, the sisters have to stop their chaotic living and face the music. It is a cozy, funny, and slightly stressful look at how families fight and love each other without ever being in the same room. You will recognize the familiar vibe of a family that loves to argue but cannot stand to be apart.

What really makes this work is the acting and the way it captures that nervous energy of family drama. The dialogue feels real, like people actually talking, not a scripted play. While the pacing is a bit slow in the middle, the emotional payoffs are worth it. If you enjoy stories about sisterhood and making peace with parents, you should definitely check this out. It is a great pick for a rainy Sunday afternoon.
endingExplained: In the end, the sisters stop fighting and finally bond over their shared love for their father. Lou does not die, which allows the family to have a fresh start. They move past their old grudges and realize that their constant phone calls were just a way to hide their fear. The movie wraps up with a feeling of hope, showing that it is never too late to fix a broken relationship with your parents.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves family dramedies and stories about sisterhood.
